digest.component_or_area: pytest timeout configuration and CI workflow hang detection
propositions: The per-test hang budget was reduced from 300s to 20s in commit 6a5c88027c5, placing it below the measured 18.7-29.93s legitimate cost of ~14 whole-tree-scan tests on coverage-instrumented CI legs, causing recurring xdist worker crashes.

With timeout_method=thread, pytest-timeout expires tests via os._exit(1) rather than pytest.fail(), causing xdist worker termination without Failed:Timeout verdicts; this makes the crash signature indistinguishable from other worker failures and hides the root cause.

The Verified gate executes workflow files from trusted main, so patchset-only changes to _build-and-test.yml timeouts are ineffective; the stale --timeout=20 CLI flag in main overrides any ini change, requiring the fix to be merged externally.

Restoring timeout=300 in both pyproject.toml ini and the two shared-tier _build-and-test.yml lanes provides ~10x headroom over measured legitimate costs and prevents worker crashes from ordinary variance and coverage startup overhead.

Under --dist loadgroup with worker crashes, pending items are re-dispatched to respawned workers that crash on the same item up to numprocesses*4 restarts, burning job time toward the 60-minute ceiling until --max-worker-restart=0 is set.
The pytest-timeout precedence hierarchy (marker > CLI > env > ini) means a conftest marker-floor mechanism can make the ini authoritative on future patchsets despite stale CLI flags in trusted main.
